note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-22). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse, or at its "from" words inside the verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words. God is not pictured, Job and his friends are not portrayed as biblical people but shown through ordinary people of today, and nothing violent is shown.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: Job's anguish, if it could be weighed, would be heavier than all the sand of the seas; he cries out because he truly suffers, as no animal cries out while it has its food, and what he is given to swallow sickens him.

sections.meaning: A man losing heart is owed loyalty, but his friends failed him like a desert stream: full and roaring when no one needs it, gone when thirsty travelers come to it, and they drew back from his ruin in fear.

sections.meaning: He never asked his friends for money or rescue; he asked only to be shown honestly where he went wrong, not to be lectured and have a despairing man's words brushed aside as wind.

candidates.prompt: On a wide empty beach under a clear sky stands a giant old iron balance scale, taller than a house. On one of its two pans sits a grey-haired man in a plain shirt, bent over with his head in his hands, and his side of the scale has sunk all the way down to the sand. The other pan, piled high with a great mountain of beach sand, is lifted high in the air. The sea stretches away behind.

On a wide beach stands a large old brass balance scale. In one pan lies a single heavy, dark, rough stone, and that pan has sunk right down. The other pan holds a great heaped mountain of pale beach sand spilling over its rim, and yet it is lifted high in the air, outweighed. The sea and an endless shore of sand stretch away behind under soft overcast light.

In a bare, dusty, sun-baked field with no grass at all, a grey donkey stands with its head thrown back and its mouth wide open, braying loudly. Beside it stands an empty wooden feed trough, completely bare. Dry cracked earth stretches away to a pale horizon under a hazy sky.

In a plain bedroom, a sick grey-haired man sits propped up in bed and turns his face away in disgust from a tray on his lap holding a plate of pale, bland food: plain boiled egg whites and a slice of dry white bread. One hand pushes the tray away. Pale grey daylight from a window.

In a dark, bare room at night lit only by one small bedside lamp, a grey-haired man in a plain shirt sits on the edge of his bed, bent forward with exhaustion, his face lifted upward and both hands held open in front of him in a desperate plea. The rest of the room is in deep shadow.

In a dim, bare room at night, an exhausted grey-haired man lies on his back on a bare mattress, staring upward with tired, pleading eyes, one open hand lifted weakly toward the ceiling. A faint cold light from a window falls across him. The room is otherwise empty.

In a quiet city park, a large bronze statue of a strong, upright man stands tall and unbending on a high stone plinth. On a park bench at the foot of the plinth, a weary grey-haired man in a plain shirt sits slumped forward, utterly spent, his arms hanging and his head low. Soft afternoon light.

On a bare hillside, a huge grey granite boulder stands solid and unmoved. Against its side an exhausted grey-haired man in a plain shirt leans with his whole body sagging, his head resting on the rock, barely able to stand. Overcast daylight.

A mountain stream in early spring, roaring full and fast between rocky banks, its water dark and churning with broken slabs of ice, deep snow still heaped along both banks and on the boulders. Bare trees and a grey winter sky above.

A wide stream bed in the hills in the blazing heat of high summer, completely bone-dry: a winding channel of bleached white stones and cracked mud where water once ran, flood debris caught high in the dry bushes along the banks. Heat haze shimmers over it under a hard bright sky.

In hot, dry desert hills under a blazing sky, a small line of tired, sunburnt hikers carrying backpacks has just reached the edge of a wide stream bed, and they stop in dismay: the channel is completely dry, nothing but bleached white stones and cracked mud. The one in front holds up an empty water bottle, and the others' faces fall.

In front of a house burnt to a blackened shell, a grey-haired man in a plain shirt sits alone on the ground in the ashes. Far back at the edge of the yard, near the road, three of his friends in everyday clothes stand together and hang back, hands over their mouths, afraid to come any nearer. Grey overcast light.

In a plain living room, a well-dressed man holds out a thick envelope of money to his weary grey-haired friend. The grey-haired man gently pushes the envelope back with one hand, shaking his head, and with his other hand takes hold of his friend's hand instead. Soft daylight from a window.

A close view at a plain wooden table: a man in a smart jacket has opened his wallet full of banknotes, and a grey-haired man's weathered hand rests gently on top of it, closing it and pushing it back across the table. The grey-haired man's face, above, looks at his friend and shakes his head. Soft window light.

At a plain kitchen table, a man in a neat shirt leans across the table lecturing, jabbing his pointing finger at the weary grey-haired man opposite him. The grey-haired man sits silent and listening, one hand pressed over his mouth, his eyes tired and searching. Plain daylight from a window.

On a wide, empty, windswept field under a grey sky, a strong gust of wind has torn loose a stack of blank white sheets of paper, and dozens of them fly and scatter away across the field and into the sky, out of reach. In the middle distance a grey-haired man in a plain shirt stands with one empty hand still reaching after them.

A close portrait of a weathered grey-haired man in a plain shirt, worn by grief, looking straight out of the picture into the viewer's eyes, steady, open and honest, nothing hidden in his face. Soft, clear daylight on his face, a plain softly blurred room behind him.

On a long, straight country road through open fields, a man in everyday clothes who had been walking away has stopped and turned back, looking over his shoulder at his weary grey-haired friend sitting alone on a stone by the roadside behind him. Clear, cool daylight.
